scope: Creative AI; no robotics or physical AI. Delta since the saved 5 October review: two fresh papers, two version-record updates, and four explicitly dated carryovers. Individual checked_at fields retain review provenance. Author evidence, not a universal SOTA ranking.

papers.title: OuroWorld: make the scene loop, not just the video.
papers.full_title: OuroWorld: Bringing Any 3D World Alive as Diverse, Endlessly Looping 3D Cinemagraphs
papers.summary: Fits generated multi-view motion to periodic 4D Gaussians. A Fourier deformation field enforces loop closure; a reference-anchored drift field absorbs inconsistent training views.
papers.caveat: Loop closure does not guarantee plausible motion. Wider viewpoints expose inconsistent supervision; evaluation covers a limited orbit, not arbitrary free navigation.
papers.change: New to the watchlist: submitted 8 October, v1. Official implementation now inspected; no model execution.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation on 39 reconstructed/generated scenes, static and ±20° orbit cameras, ground-truth-free metrics and a 30-participant study against four baselines.
papers.access: Public code and run instructions verified. README says its code is MIT but the full pipeline includes non-commercial dependencies. The default reference-video path uses paid APIs; released references and a documented Wan 2.2 alternative are options. Weights and complete runs not tested.
papers.creator_implication: A useful direction for looping backgrounds and animated 3D set pieces. Periodic deformation offers a concrete graphic without presenting a synthetic demonstration as generated footage.
papers.review_depth: Primary full-paper method, evaluation and limitations; current submission history and official repository; no reproduction

papers.title: SepGen: keep the sounds on separate tracks.
papers.full_title: SepGen: Multi-Stem Audio-Video Separation and Generation in a Single Model
papers.summary: Adds captioned audio stems to a frozen joint audio-video generator, using stem-only LoRA updates and one-way attention from the protected scene mix to stems.
papers.caveat: Trained and evaluated for two sources. Stems retain scene acoustics and resynthesized phase; the spatial demo does not establish accurate source localization or new-view acoustics.
papers.change: New to the watchlist: submitted 8 October, v1. Official inference/training repository and checkpoint links inspected; no model execution.
papers.evaluation: 194 generated two-source prompts; separation on 149 Veo scenes, 64 LTX-2.3 scenes and 172 real SAM-Audio-bench recordings. Author-reported tests.
papers.access: Public inference/training code, HF adapter links and moving-camera demo verified. README requires a 48GB NVIDIA GPU and gated LTX-2.5 access; LTX-2.x Community License applies. Precomputed training features remain pending in the README; complete training-data availability not established.
papers.creator_implication: Separate dialogue or effects can be remixed after generation. Its repository includes a CrossView-Warp IC-LoRA/depth/stereo demonstration; treat that as a demo rather than validated spatial reconstruction.
papers.review_depth: Primary full-paper method, benchmarks, ablations and limitations; current history and official repository; HF checkpoint links followed but detailed retrieval intermittent; no reproduction

papers.title: WINGS: fill the scene, then move the camera.
papers.summary: Completes masked Gaussian-splat geometry and appearance using a 3D-native prior, without inpainted reference views.
papers.caveat: Axis-aligned pattern bias and limited view-dependent appearance; not real-time. Consistency does not establish the true hidden geometry.
papers.change: Carryover, originally covered in the Oct 2 delta and Oct 5 edition. Current arXiv history still lists v1 only; no new technical release verified.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation on 29 scenes from COR-NeRF, Inpaint360 and 360-USID; user study with 29 participants and 1,401 comparisons. No independent reproduction.
papers.access: Paper available. Runnable public code/checkpoints not verified.
papers.creator_implication: A coherent scene completion could support repeated camera moves after object removal. This edition’s interactive illustrates shared synthetic geometry; it does not run WINGS.
papers.review_depth: Previous primary full-paper review; current arXiv history rechecked; no reproduction
papers.full_title: WINGS: Reference-Free Gaussian Splatting Inpainting with 3D-Native Generative Priors

papers.title: ID-Forcing: the cache remembers more than you kept.
papers.summary: Self-caching, a bounded rolling cache, an initial sink and positional rerotation address cached features whose original conditioning context has already been evicted.
papers.caveat: ID means in-distribution, not identity. The cache argument is not a guarantee that arbitrary long videos match the training distribution. Some consistency metrics can reward near-static collapse.
papers.change: Version-record update: v2 submitted 7 October at 14:51:16 UTC. No material method or result change was established in this bounded review; this is not a second model launch.
papers.evaluation: Self-Forcing and LongLive on Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B; 128 refined MovieGen prompts, 120- and 240-second videos, four denoising steps. Author-reported tests.
papers.access: Paper v2 available. Official project retrieval still failed; runnable public code availability remains unverified.
papers.creator_implication: Long-shot reliability may depend on how memory was created, as well as how much is kept. Show a cache ancestry graph and the effects of eviction.
papers.review_depth: Previous primary method/evaluation review plus current history and v2 abstract/method inspection; full v1-v2 diff not verified; no reproduction
papers.full_title: In-Distribution Forcing for Long Video Generation at Test Time

papers.title: Custom Forcing: keep the subject through a long shot.
papers.summary: Persistent reference anchors, drift-adaptive value amplification and anchor contrastive guidance preserve a subject in long autoregressive video without fine-tuning the generator.
papers.caveat: Whole-subject customization, not precise part editing; no multi-subject evaluation. Excessively strong anchoring can suppress motion or make the subject dominate the frame.
papers.change: Version-record correction: v2 was submitted 5 October at 05:25:58 UTC, before the previous edition's recorded cutoff. The Oct 5 v1-only statement was incomplete. No new technical result is claimed from this revision check.
papers.evaluation: Frozen RollingForcing/Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B; 10 DreamBooth subjects, 10 prompts each; 30-second and 2-minute outputs. Author comparisons, not universal model rankings.
papers.access: Paper v2 available. Official project retrieval failed during this check; a new runnable public code release was not verified.
papers.creator_implication: Useful research direction for keeping a prop or character recognizable across extended action. A graphic can show the tradeoff between anchoring strength, drift and motion.
papers.review_depth: Previous primary method/evaluation review plus current history and v2 abstract/method inspection; full v1-v2 diff not verified; no reproduction
papers.full_title: Custom Forcing: Training-Free Subject Customization for Autoregressive Video Generation

papers.title: PartiCam: search for a better camera path.
papers.summary: Combines global particle guidance with local refinement to guide a pretrained video generator along a requested camera path.
papers.caveat: Small evaluation; camera metrics do not all improve. Training-free still requires inference-time search. It does not establish control for arbitrary commercial video models.
papers.change: Carryover from the 5 October review; original release is not new this week. First full weekly coverage; already included in the Oct 2 delta. No later arXiv revision found.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation on nine static and nine dynamic videos using the NVS-Solver protocol, primarily CogVideo-based comparisons.
papers.access: Paper available; runnable code not verified. The author site's PartiCam project link points to an unrelated Sparfels page, so use the versioned paper link.
papers.creator_implication: A camera-path graphic can expose the competition between image quality and geometric adherence, with particle count and local-search strength as controls.
papers.review_depth: Primary abstract, method, evaluation, author project link and current version history; no reproduction
papers.full_title: PartiCam: Camera Controlled Video Generation with Reward Guidance

papers.title: Audible World Models: sound that stays in the scene.
papers.summary: Grounds generated sound sources in reconstructed scene geometry, then renders listener-dependent spatial audio.
papers.caveat: Offline construction with static geometry and fixed automatically placed sources. A supplied moving-source trajectory is not automatic motion inference or action–sound synchronization. Spatial tests measure consistency with the constructed scene.
papers.change: Carryover from the 5 October review; original release is not new this week. First full weekly coverage; already included in the Oct 2 delta. No later arXiv revision found.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation on 80 generated scenes with semantic and geometry-referenced spatial tests. Metric-dependent comparisons; not best on every semantic score.
papers.access: Paper available. Runnable public implementation not verified.
papers.creator_implication: For a camera move, sound should stay attached to its source. A listener-path diagram can distinguish generated dry audio from spatial rendering.
papers.review_depth: Primary abstract, pipeline, evaluation, ablations, limitations and current version history; no reproduction
papers.full_title: Audible World Models: Spatially Aware Sound Generation for 3D Worlds

papers.title: Adaptive diffusion: spend steps where they help.
papers.summary: A proportional-integral controller uses current and previous numerical error to choose stochastic sampling steps; averaged paths also yield fixed schedules.
papers.caveat: FFHQ, ImageNet-64 and LM1B. Per-sample adaptivity offers modest real-data gains; it does not beat every low-NFE baseline. Language perplexity gains trade against token entropy. Linked code access unverified.
papers.change: Carryover from the 5 October review; original release is not new this week. New to this edition: submitted 2 October, v1; no later revision verified.
papers.evaluation: Image FID at matched average NFE, three sets of 50,000 samples; language perplexity and unigram entropy. Also tests a 1D analytic mixture.
papers.access: Paper links https://github.com/ellakemperman/adaptive-second-order-diffusion-solvers; browser retrieval failed, so runnable access is not confirmed.
papers.creator_implication: Compare schedule and solver together at a compute budget. A large benefit in a toy distribution need not transfer to image or language models.
papers.review_depth: Primary abstract, algorithm, evaluation and limitations; no reproduction
papers.full_title: Adaptive diffusion: spend steps where they help.
